e-8592.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
e-8592.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t) =  \langle 1, \, \sqrt{2} t,\, -t^2 \rangle.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
e-8592.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a$ and $||\mathbf v||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨1,\,\sqrt{2}t,\,-{t}^{2}⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,\sqrt{2},\,-2t⟩ \\  & =2t+2{t}^{3} \\  & =2t({t}^{2}+1), \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(1)}^{2}+{(\sqrt{2}t)}^{2}+{(-{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{4}+2{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =\sqrt{{({t}^{2}+1)}^{2}} \\  & ={t}^{2}+1.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2t({t}^{2}+1)}{{t}^{2}+1} \\  & =2t.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8591.knowledge_point: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
e-8591.problem: The velocity $\mathbf v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $\mathbf v(t)= \left\langle -4, \, \cos{(2t)},\, \sin{(2t)} \right\rangle.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
e-8591.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_N = \dfrac{||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $\mathbf v \times \mathbf a{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨-4,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),\,\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\times ⟨0,\,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t),\,2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ -4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{sin}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & 2\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}-4 & \operatorname{cos}⁡(2t) \\ 0 & -2\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+2{sin}^{2}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t),8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t)⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||\mathbf v||$ and $||\mathbf v \times \mathbf a||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4)}^{2}+{(\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16+{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{16+1} \\  & =\sqrt{17}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(2)}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{cos}⁡(2t))}^{2}+{(8\operatorname{sin}⁡(2t))}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64{cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+64{sin}^{2}⁡(2t)} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64({cos}^{2}⁡(2t)+{sin}^{2}⁡(2t))} \\  & =\sqrt{4+64} \\  & =\sqrt{68} \\  & =2\sqrt{17}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2\sqrt{17}}{\sqrt{17}} \\  & =2.\end{aligned}
$$

e-8593.knowledge_point: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment
e-8593.problem: The position $\mathbf r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)= \langle e^{2t}, \, e^{-t} , \, 1 \rangle,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t = 0\,\textrm s.$
e-8593.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
a_T = \dfrac{\mathbf v \cdot \mathbf a}{||\mathbf v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t = 0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨2{e}^{2t},\,-{e}^{-t},\,0⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨2{e}^{2(0)},\,-{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t = 0{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2{e}^{2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{-t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨4{e}^{2t},\,{e}^{-t},\,0,⟩ \\ a(0) & =⟨4{e}^{2(0)},\,{e}^{-0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $\mathbf v(0) \cdot \mathbf a(0)$ and $||\mathbf v(0)||\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨2,\,-1,\,0⟩\cdot ⟨4,\,1,\,0⟩ \\  & =7, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(2)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{7}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & =\frac{7\sqrt{5}}{5}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\dfrac{7\sqrt{5}}{5} \, \textrm{ms}^{-2}.$

before.html:
Question 1
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨et,−2e−2t,1⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
et−2e−2tet+2e−2t+1
b
 e2t−8e−4te2t+4e−4t+1
c
 et−8e−2te2t+4e−4t
d
 e2t−e−2te2t+e−2t
e
 et+e−2tet+1
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiate to obtain a(t)=⟨e^t,4e^{-2t},0⟩. Then v·a=e^{2t}-8e^{-4t} and ||v||=√(e^{2t}+4e^{-4t}+1). Thus a_T=(v·a)/||v||, which is option b.

after.name: Question 1
after.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩ \\  & ={e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(2{e}^{-2t})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 1
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨et,−2e−2t,1⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
et−2e−2tet+2e−2t+1
b
 e2t−8e−4te2t+4e−4t+1
c
 et−8e−2te2t+4e−4t
d
 e2t−e−2te2t+e−2t
e
 et+e−2tet+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−2e−2t),ddt(1)⟩=⟨et,4e−2t,0⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||:

v⋅a=⟨et,−2e−2t,1⟩⋅⟨et,4e−2t,0⟩=e2t−8e−4t,||v||=(et)2+(2e−2t)2+12=e2t+4e−4t+1.

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=e2t−8e−4te2t+4e−4t+1.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-2{e}^{-2t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-2{e}^{-2t},\,1⟩\cdot ⟨{e}^{t},\,4{e}^{-2t},\,0⟩ \\  & ={e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{({e}^{t})}^{2}+{(2{e}^{-2t})}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}-8{e}^{-4t}}{\sqrt{{e}^{2t}+4{e}^{-4t}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t3,t2⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
 6t+42+9t4+4t2
b
 18t2+44+3t2+2t
c
 18t3+4t4+9t4+4t2
d
6t32+3t2+2t2
e
 3t24+6t4+2t2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives v(t)=⟨2,3t²,2t⟩ and a(t)=⟨0,6t,2⟩. Thus v·a=18t³+4t and ||v||=√(4+9t⁴+4t²). The tangential component a_T=(v·a)/||v|| matches option c.

after.name: Question 2
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{3},\,{t}^{2}⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨2,\,3{t}^{2},\,2t⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,6t,\,2⟩ \\  & =18{t}^{3}+4t \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(3{t}^{2})^{2}+(2t)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{18{t}^{3}+4t}{\sqrt{4+9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 3
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
te2t(t2+1)e2t+16
b
(t2+1)e2te2t+16
c
(t+1)e2tt2+16
d
e2tt2+16
e
(t2+t+1)e2t(t2+1)e2t+16
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t)=⟨(t+1)e^t,−e^t,0⟩. Hence v·a=(t²+t+1)e^{2t} and ||v||=√((t²+1)e^{2t}+16). Therefore a_T=(v·a)/||v|| is option e.

after.name: Question 3
after.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩\cdot ⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =t(t+1){e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+0, \\  & =({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.html:
Question 3
?

The velocity v of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the tangential component of acceleration at time t.

a
te2t(t2+1)e2t+16
b
(t2+1)e2te2t+16
c
(t+1)e2tt2+16
d
e2tt2+16
e
(t2+t+1)e2t(t2+1)e2t+16
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows: a=⟨ddt(tet),ddt(−et),ddt(4)⟩=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩

Next, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨tet,−et,4⟩⋅⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩=t(t+1)e2t+e2t+0,=(t2+t+1)e2t,||v||=(tet)2+(−et)2+(4)2=t2e2t+e2t+16=(t2+1)e2t+16

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=(t2+t+1)e2t(t2+1)e2t+16.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the tangential component of acceleration at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we need to compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩\cdot ⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =t(t+1){e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+0, \\  & =({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(t{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(4)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}+16} \\  & =\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{({t}^{2}+t+1){e}^{2t}}{\sqrt{({t}^{2}+1){e}^{2t}+16}}.\end{aligned}
$$

before.html:
Question 4
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨cos⁡4t,sin⁡4t,3t⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
4
b
0
c
3
d
35
e
45
Submit

decision.explanation: The velocity is ⟨−4sin(4t),4cos(4t),3⟩, whose speed is √(16sin²(4t)+16cos²(4t)+9)=5. Since speed is constant, the tangential acceleration is d||v||/dt=0, giving option b.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,3t⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3)⟩ \\  & =⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨-16\operatorname{cos}⁡4t,\,-16\operatorname{sin}⁡4t,\,0⟩ \\  & =64\operatorname{sin}⁡4t\operatorname{cos}⁡4t-64\operatorname{cos}⁡4t\operatorname{sin}⁡4t \\  & =0 \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(-4\operatorname{sin}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(4\operatorname{cos}⁡4t)}^{2}+{(3)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{16{sin}^{2}⁡4t+16{cos}^{2}⁡4t+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16({sin}^{2}⁡4t+{cos}^{2}⁡4t)+9} \\  & =\sqrt{16+9} \\  & =\sqrt{25} \\  & =5\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{0}{5} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 4
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨cos⁡4t,sin⁡4t,3t⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
4
b
0
c
3
d
35
e
45
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(cos⁡4t),ddt(sin⁡4t),ddt(3t)⟩=⟨−4sin⁡4t,4cos⁡4t,3⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(−4sin⁡4t),ddt(4cos⁡4t),ddt(3)⟩=⟨−16cos⁡4t,−16sin⁡4t,0⟩

Then, we compute v⋅a and ||v||: v⋅a=⟨−4sin⁡4t,4cos⁡4t,3⟩⋅⟨−16cos⁡4t,−16sin⁡4t,0⟩=64sin⁡4tcos⁡4t−64cos⁡4tsin⁡4t=0||v||=(−4sin⁡4t)2+(4cos⁡4t)2+(3)2=16sin2⁡4t+16cos2⁡4t+9=16(sin2⁡4t+cos2⁡4t)+9=16+9=25=5

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get aT=v⋅a||v||=05=0.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution declares a_T=0, matching option b and the independent calculation: v·a=0 and ||v||=5, so a_T=0/5=0. The incorrect feedback refers to the deliberately submitted option a.

Question 5
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨ln⁡t,1t,−1⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
t2t2+1
b
−t2+2t3t2+1
c
2t2+3t2t2+4
d
−t+2t3t2+4
e
−2tt2+1
Submit

decision.explanation: For t>0, v=⟨1/t,−1/t²,0⟩ and a=⟨−1/t²,2/t³,0⟩. Thus v·a=−(t²+2)/t⁵ and ||v||=√(t²+1)/t². Their quotient is −(t²+2)/(t³√(t²+1)), matching option b.

after.name: Question 5
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,-1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{t}^{5}} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}} \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}})} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{3}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 5
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨ln⁡t,1t,−1⟩. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
t2t2+1
b
−t2+2t3t2+1
c
2t2+3t2t2+4
d
−t+2t3t2+4
e
−2tt2+1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(ln⁡t),ddt(1t),ddt(−1)⟩=⟨1t,−1t2,0⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(1t),ddt(−1t2),ddt(0)⟩=⟨−1t2,2t3,0⟩

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Tangental Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,\frac{1}{t},\,-1⟩.$ Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-1)⟩ \\  & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\frac{1}{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v\cdot a$ and $||v||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\cdot a & =⟨\frac{1}{t},\,-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,0⟩\cdot ⟨-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}},\,\frac{2}{{t}^{3}},\,0⟩ \\  & =-\frac{1}{{t}^{3}}-\frac{2}{{t}^{5}} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}} \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(\frac{1}{t})}^{2}+{(-\frac{1}{{t}^{2}})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{1}{{t}^{2}}+\frac{1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\sqrt{\frac{{t}^{2}+1}{{t}^{4}}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{(-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{5}})}{(\frac{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}{{t}^{2}})} \\  & =-\frac{{t}^{2}+2}{{t}^{3}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+1}}.\end{aligned}
$$

after.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$

$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,3⟩\times ⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-\operatorname{cos}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{sin}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & 3 \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}\operatorname{sin}⁡t & -\operatorname{cos}⁡t \\ \operatorname{cos}⁡t & \operatorname{sin}⁡t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨-3\operatorname{sin}⁡t,3\operatorname{cos}⁡t,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

$$

$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$

before.html:
Question 7
?

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
tett2+2
b
te2tt2+2t+2
c
1ett2+2
d
ett2+2t+2
e
ett2+2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating position gives v=⟨(t+1)e^t,−e^t,0⟩ and a=⟨(t+2)e^t,−e^t,0⟩. Thus v×a=⟨0,0,e^{2t}⟩ and ||v||=e^t√(t²+2t+2). Therefore a_N=||v×a||/||v||=e^t/√(t²+2t+2), matching option d.

after.name: Question 7
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\times ⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ (t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 0 \\ -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,{e}^{2t}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{((t+1){e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{({e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

The position r of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨tet,−et,4⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
tett2+2
b
te2tt2+2t+2
c
1ett2+2
d
ett2+2t+2
e
ett2+2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(tet),ddt(−et),ddt(4)⟩=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt((t+1)et),ddt(−et),ddt(0)⟩=⟨(t+2)et,−et,0⟩

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨(t+1)et,−et,0⟩×⟨(t+2)et,−et,0⟩=ijk(t+1)et−et0(t+2)et−et0= −et0−et0i−(t+1)et0(t+2)et0j+(t+1)et−et(t+2)et−etk=⟨0,0,e2t⟩,||v||=((t+1)et)2+(−et)2+(0)2=(t+1)2e2t+e2t=ett2+2t+2,||v×a||=(0)2+(0)2+(e2t)2=e2t

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get aN=||v×a||||v||=e2tett2+2t+2=ett2+2t+2.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨t{e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,4⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(4)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}((t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨(t+1){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩\times ⟨(t+2){e}^{t},\,-{e}^{t},\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ (t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-{e}^{t} & 0 \\ -{e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & 0 \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t} \\ (t+2){e}^{t} & -{e}^{t}\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,{e}^{2t}⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{((t+1){e}^{t})}^{2}+{(-{e}^{t})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(t+1)^{2}{e}^{2t}+{e}^{2t}} \\  & ={e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{({e}^{2t})}^{2}} \\  & ={e}^{2t}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{2t}}{{e}^{t}\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}} \\  & =\frac{{e}^{t}}{\sqrt{{t}^{2}+2t+2}}.\end{aligned}
$$

a
3

313

9

913

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives v=⟨3cos(3t),−3sin(3t),2⟩ and a=⟨−9sin(3t),−9cos(3t),0⟩. Since v·a=0, acceleration is entirely normal. Thus a_N=||a||=9, matching option c.

after.name: Question 8
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,2t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\times ⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27{cos}^{2}⁡3t-27{sin}^{2}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27⟩ \\  & =9⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-3⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡3t+9{sin}^{2}⁡3t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4} \\  & =\sqrt{13}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =9\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3)}^{2}} \\  & =9\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡3t+4{sin}^{2}⁡3t+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}

EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(sin⁡3t),ddt(cos⁡3t),ddt(2t)⟩=⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,2⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(3cos⁡3t),ddt(−3sin⁡3t),ddt(2)⟩=⟨−9sin⁡3t,−9cos⁡3t,0⟩

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨3cos⁡3t,−3sin⁡3t,2⟩×⟨−9sin⁡3t,−9cos⁡3t,0⟩=ijk3cos⁡3t−3sin⁡3t2−9sin⁡3t−9cos⁡3t0= −3sin⁡3t2−9cos⁡3t0i−3cos⁡3t2−9sin⁡3t0j+3cos⁡3t−3sin⁡3t−9sin⁡3t−9cos⁡3tk=⟨18cos⁡3t,−18sin⁡3t,−27cos2⁡3t−27sin2⁡3t⟩=⟨18cos⁡3t,−18sin⁡3t,−27⟩=9⟨2cos⁡3t,−2sin⁡3t,−3⟩,||v||=(3cos⁡3t)2+(−3sin⁡3t)2+(2)2=9cos2⁡3t+9sin2⁡3t+4=9(cos2⁡3t+sin2⁡3t)+4=9+4=13,||v×a||=9(2cos⁡3t)2+(−2sin⁡3t)2+(−3)2=94cos2⁡3t+4sin2⁡3t+9=94(cos2⁡3t+sin2⁡3t)+9=94+9=913

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get aN=||v×a||||v||=91313=9.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,2t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,2⟩\times ⟨-9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,\,-9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & 2 \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t & -3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t \\ -9\operatorname{sin}⁡3t & -9\operatorname{cos}⁡3t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27{cos}^{2}⁡3t-27{sin}^{2}⁡3t⟩ \\  & =⟨18\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-18\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-27⟩ \\  & =9⟨2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t,-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t,-3⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(3\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(2)}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{cos}^{2}⁡3t+9{sin}^{2}⁡3t+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+4} \\  & =\sqrt{9+4} \\  & =\sqrt{13}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =9\sqrt{{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡3t)}^{2}+{(-3)}^{2}} \\  & =9\sqrt{4{cos}^{2}⁡3t+4{sin}^{2}⁡3t+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡3t+{sin}^{2}⁡3t)+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{4+9} \\  & =9\sqrt{13}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{9\sqrt{13}}{\sqrt{13}} \\  & =9.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 9

The velocity v of a particle P at time t>0 is given by v(t)=⟨2t,t2,0⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
t1+4t
b
t24+t2
c
t2+11+4t
d
2t4+t2
e
t+14+t2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a=⟨2,2t,0⟩. Then v×a=⟨0,0,2t²⟩ and, since t>0, ||v||=t√(4+t²). Thus a_N=||v×a||/||v||=2t/√(4+t²), matching option d.

after.name: Question 9
after.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & {t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & {t}^{2} \\ 2 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,4{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,2{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+({t}^{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(4+{t}^{2})} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{1}+(0)^{2}+(2{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

content.problem: The velocity $v$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $v(t)=⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0)⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute $v\times a:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & {t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & {t}^{2} \\ 2 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,4{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,2{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+({t}^{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(4+{t}^{2})} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{1}+(0)^{2}+(2{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,{t}^{2},\,0⟩\times ⟨2,\,2t,\,0⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & {t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2 & 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}{t}^{2} & 0 \\ 2t & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & {t}^{2} \\ 2 & 2t\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,0,4{t}^{2}-2{t}^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨0,0,2{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}||v|| & =\sqrt{(2t)^{2}+({t}^{2})^{2}+(0)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{2}+{t}^{4}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(4+{t}^{2})} \\  & =t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}} \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{1}+(0)^{2}+(2{t}^{2})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{4{t}^{4}} \\  & =2{t}^{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{2{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}} \\  & =\frac{2t}{\sqrt{4+{t}^{2}}}.\end{aligned}
$$

c
2t23t2+1

6t9t2+4

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives v=⟨2t,0,−3t²⟩ and a=⟨2,0,−6t⟩. Thus v×a=⟨0,6t²,0⟩ and ||v||=t√(9t²+4), since t>0. Therefore a_N=||v×a||/||v||=6t/√(9t²+4), matching option e.

after.name: Question 10
after.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,-6,\,-{t}^{3}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-6),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,-(-12{t}^{2}+6{t}^{2}),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,6{t}^{2},0⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(9{t}^{2}+4)} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(6{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6t}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 10
?

The position r of a particle P at time t>0 is given by r(t)=⟨t2,−6,−t3⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t.

a
t29t2+4
b
3t3t2+1
c
2t23t2+1
d
2t+39t2+4
e
6t9t2+4
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows: v=⟨ddt(t2),ddt(−6),ddt(−t3)⟩=⟨2t,0,−3t2⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector: a=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(0),ddt(−3t2)⟩=⟨2,0,−6t⟩

Now, we compute v×a,||v|| and ||v×a||:

v×a=⟨2t,0,−3t2⟩×⟨2,0,−6t⟩=ijk2t0−3t220−6t= 0−3t20−6ti−2t−3t22−6tj+2t020k=⟨0,−(−12t2+6t2),0⟩=⟨0,6t2,0⟩,||v||=(2t)2+(0)2+(−3t2)2=9t4+4t2=t2(9t2+4)=t9t2+4,||v×a||=(0)2+(6t2)2+(0)2=6t2

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get aN=||v×a||||v||=6t2t9t2+4=6t9t2+4.

content.knowledge_point: Finding the Normal Component of  Acceleration Given a Position or Velocity
content.problem: The position $r$ of a particle $P$ at time $t>0$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{t}^{2},\,-6,\,-{t}^{3}⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t.$
content.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector, as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-6),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-{t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(0),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we compute $v\times a,||v||$ and $||v\times a||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v\times a & =⟨2t,\,0,\,-3{t}^{2}⟩\times ⟨2,\,0,\,-6t⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 2t & 0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\text{ }\left|\begin{aligned}0 & -3{t}^{2} \\ 0 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}2t & -3{t}^{2} \\ 2 & -6t\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}2t & 0 \\ 2 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨0,-(-12{t}^{2}+6{t}^{2}),0⟩ \\  & =⟨0,6{t}^{2},0⟩, \\ ||v|| & =\sqrt{{(2t)}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}+{(-3{t}^{2})}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9{t}^{4}+4{t}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{{t}^{2}(9{t}^{2}+4)} \\  & =t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}, \\ ||v\times a|| & =\sqrt{{(0)}^{2}+{(6{t}^{2})}^{2}+{(0)}^{2}} \\  & =6{t}^{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||} \\  & =\frac{6{t}^{2}}{t\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}} \\  & =\frac{6t}{\sqrt{9{t}^{2}+4}}.\end{aligned}
$$

Question 11
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨et,−tet,2t⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=0s.

a
4ms−2
b
64ms−2
c
3ms−2
d
6ms−2
e
62ms−2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives v(0)=⟨1,−1,2⟩ and a(0)=⟨1,−2,0⟩. Therefore a_T=(v·a)/||v||=3/√6=√6/2 m s⁻², matching option e.

after.name: Question 11
after.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨{e}^{t},\,-t{e}^{t},\,2t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-t{e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2t)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+1){e}^{t},\,2⟩, \\ v(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+1){e}^{0},\,2⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=0:$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-(t+1){e}^{t}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2)⟩ \\  & =⟨{e}^{t},\,-(t+2){e}^{t},\,0⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨{e}^{0},\,-(0+2){e}^{0},\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\cdot a(0)$ and $||v(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\cdot a(0) & =⟨1,\,-1,\,2⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,-2,\,0⟩ \\  & =3, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{(1)^{2}+(-1)^{2}+(2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{6}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(0)\cdot a(0)}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{6}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $\frac{\sqrt{6}}{2}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

after.html:
Question 11
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨et,−tet,2t⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=0s.

a
4ms−2
b
64ms−2
c
3ms−2
d
6ms−2
e
62ms−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=0, as follows: v=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−tet),ddt(2t)⟩=⟨et,−(t+1)et,2⟩,v(0)=⟨e0,−(0+1)e0,2⟩=⟨1,−1,2⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=0: a=⟨ddt(et),ddt(−(t+1)et),ddt(2)⟩=⟨et,−(t+2)et,0⟩,a(0)=⟨e0,−(0+2)e0,0⟩=⟨1,−2,0⟩

Then, we compute v(0)⋅a(0) and ||v(0)||:

v(0)⋅a(0)=⟨1,−1,2⟩⋅⟨1,−2,0⟩=3,||v(0)||=(1)2+(−1)2+(2)2=6

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=0, and we get aT=v(0)⋅a(0)||v(0)||=36=62.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 62ms−2.

before.html:
Question 12
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t,t3⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=1s.

a
 36ms−2
b
 33ms−2
c
 26ms−2
d
 93ms−2
e
 3ms−2
Submit

decision.explanation: At t=1, v=⟨√2,1,3⟩ and a=⟨0,0,6⟩. Thus a_T=(v·a)/||v||=18/√12=3√3 m s⁻², matching option b.

after.name: Question 12
after.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\sqrt{2}t,\,t,\,{t}^{3}⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}({t}^{3})⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3{t}^{2}⟩ \\ v(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3(1)^{2}⟩ \\  & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=1$:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩ \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩ \\  & =18 \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $3\sqrt{3}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

after.html:
Question 12
?

The position r, in meters, of a particle P at time t is given by r(t)=⟨2t,t,t3⟩, where t is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of P at time t=1s.

a
 36ms−2
b
 33ms−2
c
 26ms−2
d
 93ms−2
e
 3ms−2
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

The tangential component of acceleration is given by aT=v⋅a||v||.

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: v=⟨ddt(2t),ddt(t),ddt(t3)⟩=⟨2,1,3t2⟩v(1)=⟨2,1,3(1)2⟩=⟨2,1,3⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at t=1: a=⟨ddt(2),ddt(1),ddt(3t2)⟩=⟨0,0,6t⟩a(1)=⟨0,0,6(1)⟩=⟨0,0,6⟩.

Then, we compute v(1)⋅a(1) and ||v(1)||:

v(1)⋅a(1)=⟨2,1,3⟩⋅⟨0,0,6⟩=18||v(1)||=(2)2+12+32=12=23

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at t=1, and we get aT=v(1)⋅a(1)||v(1)||=1823=33.

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is 33ms−2.

verification.explanation: The revealed solution declares 3√3 m s⁻², matching option b. Independently, v(1)=⟨√2,1,3⟩ and a(1)=⟨0,0,6⟩, so a_T=18/√12=3√3. The incorrect feedback concerns the deliberately submitted option d.

\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\sqrt{2}),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(3{t}^{2})⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6t⟩ \\ a(1) & =⟨0,\,0,\,6(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\cdot a(1)$ and $||v(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\cdot a(1) & =⟨\sqrt{2},\,1,\,3⟩\cdot ⟨0,\,0,\,6⟩ \\  & =18 \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{(\sqrt{2})^{2}+{1}^{2}+{3}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{12} \\  & =2\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=1$, and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(1)\cdot a(1)}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{18}{2\sqrt{3}} \\  & =3\sqrt{3}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $3\sqrt{3}\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

Question 13

The velocity v, in meters per second, of a particle P at time t is given by v(t)=⟨1,cos⁡t,sin⁡t⟩. Find the normal component of the acceleration of P at time t=0s.

a
2ms−2
b
2ms−2
c
22ms−2
d
1ms−2
e
12ms−2
Submit

decision.explanation: Differentiating gives a(t)=⟨0,−sin(t),cos(t)⟩. At t=0, v=⟨1,1,0⟩ and a=⟨0,0,1⟩. They are perpendicular, so acceleration is entirely normal and a_N=||a||=1 m s⁻², matching option d.

after.name: Question 13
after.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨1,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=0\,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(0):$

$$
v(0)=⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=0,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{sin}⁡t)⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,\operatorname{cos}⁡t⟩, \\ a(0) & =⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(0)\times a(0),||v(0)||,$ and $||v(0)\times a(0)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(0)\times a(0) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}, \\ ||v(0)\times a(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(0)\times a(0)||}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $1\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

a

b

d
1ms−2
e
12ms−2
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||.

First, we evaluate v(0): v(0)=⟨1,1,0⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at t=0, as follows: a=⟨ddt(1),ddt(cos⁡t),ddt(sin⁡t)⟩=⟨0,−sin⁡t,cos⁡t⟩,a(0)=⟨0,0,1⟩

Then, we compute v(0)×a(0),||v(0)||, and ||v(0)×a(0)||:

v(0)×a(0)=⟨1,1,0⟩×⟨0,0,1⟩=ijk110001=1001i−1001j+1100k=⟨1,−1,0⟩,||v(0)||=12+12+02=2,||v(0)×a(0)||=12+(−1)2+02=2

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at t=0, and we get aN=||v(0)×a(0)||||v(0)||=22=1.

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is 1ms−2.

\begin{aligned}v(0)\times a(0) & =⟨1,\,1,\,0⟩\times ⟨0,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 1 & 1 & 0 \\ 0 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 0 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}1 & 1 \\ 0 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨1,-1,0⟩, \\ ||v(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+{1}^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}, \\ ||v(0)\times a(0)|| & =\sqrt{{1}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{0}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=0,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(0)\times a(0)||}{||v(0)||} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is $1\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

after.name: Question 14
after.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\pi \,\text{s}.$
after.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩, \\ v(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩, \\ a(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )$ and $||v(\pi )||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi ) & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =0, \\ ||v(\pi )|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )}{||v(\pi )||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment
content.problem: The position $r,$ in meters, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $r(t)=⟨\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,t⟩,$ where $t$ is measured in seconds. Find the tangential component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=\pi \,\text{s}.$
content.worked_solution:
The tangential component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{T}=\frac{v\cdot a}{||v||}.
$$

First, we compute the velocity vector by differentiating the position vector and evaluating it at $t=\pi ,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}v & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,1⟩, \\ v(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,1⟩ \\  & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and it evaluating at $t=\pi :$

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{sin}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{cos}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(1)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡t,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡t,\,0⟩, \\ a(\pi ) & =⟨-\operatorname{cos}⁡\pi ,\,\operatorname{sin}⁡\pi ,\,0⟩ \\  & =⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )$ and $||v(\pi )||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi ) & =⟨0,\,1,\,1⟩\cdot ⟨1,\,0,\,0⟩ \\  & =0, \\ ||v(\pi )|| & =\sqrt{(0)^{2}+(1)^{2}+(1)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{2}\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the tangential component of the acceleration at $t=\pi ,$ and we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{T} & =\frac{v(\pi )\cdot a(\pi )}{||v(\pi )||} \\  & =\frac{0}{\sqrt{2}} \\  & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the tangential component of the acceleration is $0\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

after.name: Question 15
after.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s},$ rounded to one decimal place.
after.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{t},\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{0)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & ≈1.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is approximately 
 $1.3\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$

c
1.7ms−2

Correct
EXPLANATION

The normal component of acceleration is given by aN=||v×a||||v||.

First, we evaluate v(1): v(1)=⟨0,2,1⟩

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at t=1, as follows: a=⟨ddt(−ln⁡t),ddt(2),ddt(t)⟩=⟨−1t,0,1⟩,a(1)=⟨−1,0,1⟩

Then, we compute v(1)×a(1),||v(1)||, and ||v(1)×a(1)||: v(1)×a(1)=⟨0,2,1⟩×⟨−1,0,1⟩=ijk021−101=2101i−01−11j+02−10k=⟨2,−1,2⟩,||v(1)||=0)2+22+12=5,||v(1)×a(1)||=22+(−1)2+22=9=3

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at t=1, and we get aN=||v(1)×a(1)||||v(1)||=35≈1.3.

content.knowledge_point: Calculating Components of Acceleration at a Particular Moment
content.problem: The velocity $v,$ in meters per second, of a particle $P$ at time $t$ is given by $v(t)=⟨-\operatorname{ln}⁡t,\,2,\,t⟩.$ Find the normal component of the acceleration of $P$ at time $t=1\,\text{s},$ rounded to one decimal place.
content.worked_solution:
The normal component of acceleration is given by

$$
{a}_{N}=\frac{||v\times a||}{||v||}.
$$

First, we evaluate $v(1):$

$$
v(1)=⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩
$$

Next, we compute the acceleration vector by differentiating the velocity vector and evaluating it at $t=1,$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a & =⟨\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(-\operatorname{ln}⁡t),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2),\,\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t)⟩ \\  & =⟨-\frac{1}{t},\,0,\,1⟩, \\ a(1) & =⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we compute $v(1)\times a(1),||v(1)||,$ and $||v(1)\times a(1)||:$

$$
\begin{aligned}v(1)\times a(1) & =⟨0,\,2,\,1⟩\times ⟨-1,\,0,\,1⟩ \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}i & j & k \\ 0 & 2 & 1 \\ -1 & 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right| \\  & =\left|\begin{aligned}2 & 1 \\ 0 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,i-\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ -1 & 1\end{aligned}\right|\,j+\left|\begin{aligned}0 & 2 \\ -1 & 0\end{aligned}\right|\,k \\  & =⟨2,-1,2⟩, \\ ||v(1)|| & =\sqrt{0)^{2}+{2}^{2}+{1}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{5}, \\ ||v(1)\times a(1)|| & =\sqrt{{2}^{2}+(-1)^{2}+{2}^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{9} \\  & =3\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we calculate the normal component of the acceleration at $t=1,$ and we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{a}_{N} & =\frac{||v(1)\times a(1)||}{||v(1)||} \\  & =\frac{3}{\sqrt{5}} \\  & ≈1.3.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the normal component of acceleration is approximately 
 $1.3\,{\text{ms}}^{-2}.$
